finding: No fonts are embedded. Every glyph depends on device fonts, so the same file shows different coverage on your Mac, iPad, and any other machine, and nothing in the app reports it.
recommendation: Adopt an embedded coverage tier (see Glyph coverage strategy).

finding: Missing glyphs are indistinguishable from real ones. Unsupported characters render as blank boxes or replacement shapes with no indication.
recommendation: Add glyph detection: render each character with the chosen stack followed by Adobe Blank 2 (1.5 KB, zero-width glyph for every code point) and flag cells whose ink box is empty. Show per-block coverage in the status bar.

finding: Font stacks in `config/fonts.json` put CJK fonts first, so Latin, IPA, and Greek render in CJK fonts' secondary designs. Two families do not exist as written (`'Noto Serif CJK'`, `'Noto Sans Mono CJK'` need a region suffix such as `SC`). No historic-script or symbol families are named (for example Segoe UI Historic, Segoe UI Symbol, Apple Symbols, Noto Sans Symbols 2).
recommendation: Replace flat stacks with script-aware composite families: `@font-face` rules using `local()` sources and `unicode-range` so each script reaches its best font. Generate them from a manifest.

finding: 2,543 combining marks are shown bare, so they render detached or invisibly. 26 default-ignorable characters (soft hyphen, combining grapheme joiner, Hangul fillers, Mongolian variation selectors) and line/paragraph separators appear as blank cells.
recommendation: Render combining marks on U+25CC DOTTED CIRCLE, as Unicode's own code charts do. Show invisible characters as labelled dashed boxes (for example "SHY", "CGJ").

finding: The page is fixed to `lang="en"`. Han characters shared by Chinese, Japanese, and Korean take their shape from the language tag, so users cannot compare regional forms.
recommendation: Add a CJK glyph-locale selector (zh-Hans, zh-Hant, zh-HK, ja, ko) that sets `lang` on the output container.

finding: Fixed 2em grid cells clip wide glyphs such as cuneiform and some pictographs. There is no text versus emoji presentation control.
recommendation: Allow cells to grow to the glyph's width. Add a presentation toggle using VS15/VS16 or `font-variant-emoji`.

finding: Unicode 18.0 is current. It adds 7 blocks and 13,007 characters (Bengali Supplement, Archaic Cuneiform Numerals, Jurchen, Jurchen Radicals, Musical Symbols Supplement, Miscellaneous Symbols and Arrows Extended, Seal). The build hard-codes the `17.0.0` URL, and `blocks.js` is maintained by hand.
recommendation: Make the Unicode version a single build input. Generate the block list from `Blocks.txt` plus a small committed category-assignment file. Then upgrade to 18.0 as a data-track release.

finding: `isNonVisible()` is a hand-written approximation that disagrees with Unicode's own properties (finding GLY-04). It also contains dead conditions: the private-use high-surrogate test is already covered by the surrogate test, and the noncharacter test appears twice.
recommendation: Derive visibility at build time from General_Category, `Default_Ignorable_Code_Point`, and `Prepended_Concatenation_Mark`. Embed it as a compact range table.

finding: `ALGO_RANGES` is maintained by hand. Its Nushu, Khitan, and CJK compatibility entries are redundant, because those characters are individually named in `UnicodeData.txt`. Unicode 18's new ranges will need new rules.
recommendation: Derive algorithmic ranges from the `<…, First>`/`<…, Last>` markers in `UnicodeData.txt`. Strip pattern-derivable names from the embedded table to save space.

finding: Search covers names only. It ignores the 481 formal name aliases (39 corrections, 354 abbreviations such as NBSP and ZWJ), and does not accept a code point (`U+1F600`, `1F600`) or a pasted character.
recommendation: Index aliases, and add code-point and literal-character lookup.

finding: No per-character properties are shown.
recommendation: Add a detail panel with General Category, Script, Age (the version that added the character), and decomposition. Age is especially useful because recently added characters are the least likely to have fonts.

finding: The build fails open. If the `UnicodeData.txt` download fails, it logs a warning and still writes `Unicode.html` with empty names and reserved-range tables, then exits successfully.
recommendation: Fail the build on any data error. Never write a degraded artifact.

finding: The build downloads Unicode data at build time with no pinned checksum. It reproduced today only because the upstream file has not changed.
recommendation: Vendor the required UCD files under `data/ucd/<version>/` with a SHA-256 manifest. The build reads them offline and verifies hashes.

finding: No tests, no CI workflow, and no artifact verification. The only check is a 400 KB size message that never fails.
recommendation: Adopt the History build chain: typecheck, standards lint, unit tests, bundle, minify, verify, with end-to-end tests as a separate CI job.

finding: The committed `Unicode.html` has no check that it matches its source.
recommendation: Add a regeneration check in CI (the History repo's `check_regenerated` pattern), or build to `dist/` and attach the file to tagged releases.

finding: Custom regex CSS and HTML minifiers, against the standards' preference for maintained libraries.
recommendation: Use `vite-plugin-singlefile` plus `html-minifier-terser`, as History does.

finding: The LZString runtime library is bundled only to unpack names.
recommendation: Use the browser's built-in `DecompressionStream("deflate-raw")`. Measured: 273 KB embedded versus 332 KB today, and one fewer dependency.

finding: `docs/CODING-STANDARDS.md` §0 maps every layer role to unused Replit scaffold paths (`artifacts/*/src/components/**` and similar). `unicode-src/` is not mapped, so no rule governs the actual application. It also declares a "multi-artifact repo" rather than the standalone HTML5 target, and says "semantic versioning" where History's copy of the same v2.2 standards requires four-part versioning. The two derived copies have drifted.
recommendation: Re-propagate the canonical v2.2 text from the programming Project wiki, then fill in §0 for this app (proposed mapping below). Add a check that flags drift between derived copies.

finding: Runtime code is ten concatenated global scripts with hidden cross-file dependencies. For example, `hex4` is defined in `charnames.js` but used in `00-classify.js`, and `tableSortState` is declared in the table renderer but reset in the render core. DOM work and logic are mixed. `renderOutput` (about 55 lines) and `buildSidebar` (about 85 lines) exceed the 20-line function limit.
recommendation: Migrate to TypeScript ES modules: pure Unicode logic under domain directories, with views on top. Extract the misplaced logic first, then split files (standards §16.2).

finding: The repository carries an unrelated Replit template: an Express API server that only streams the HTML file (with open CORS), a React/shadcn mockup sandbox (about 50 components), a Drizzle/Postgres package with an empty schema, and OpenAPI client generation. The post-merge script runs a database push. None of it is used by the app.
recommendation: Remove it, and adopt History's lean single-package layout (Vite plus `vite-plugin-singlefile`, Vitest, Playwright).

finding: There is no README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, `AGENTS.md`, or `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The repository is public but unlicensed, which legally means all rights reserved.
recommendation: Add all five. Use MIT for code, with font licenses carried separately (see Licensing).

finding: State does not survive a reload, although the standards allow URL-fragment state.
recommendation: Encode selected blocks, mode, font, and size in `location.hash`.

finding: `.agents/skills/agent-tools` is a third-party skill that grants agents `Bash(infsh *)` access to an external AI service, which this project does not use.
recommendation: Remove `.agents/` and `skills-lock.json` unless they are deliberately used.

finding: `docs/tasks/` holds 70 task files with overlapping names (`task-N.md` alongside descriptive duplicates).
recommendation: Keep them as history (standards §16.8), but add an index and stop auto-copying from `.local/tasks`.

finding: 84 of 93 commits use a Replit noreply email that does not link to the GitHub account.
recommendation: Configure the `50533494+tyohDeveloper@users.noreply.github.com` identity for future commits. Leave history as is.

finding: Selecting all blocks renders 163,807 cells. Measured: 19.2 s of frozen page in Grid mode and 23.3 s in Table mode, with 819,723 elements in the table. Each cell gets its own click handler and a tooltip name lookup at creation.
recommendation: Virtualize: fixed-size cells make windowed rendering simple. Use a single delegated click handler and compute tooltips on hover. Target under 100 ms for any selection.

finding: Every checkbox change re-renders the whole output.
recommendation: Render incrementally per block, reusing block sections already built.

finding: The display-mode and font selectors are radio buttons hidden with `display:none`, so keyboard users cannot reach them. Verified: the tab order skips them entirely.
recommendation: Hide them visually but keep them focusable, or use buttons with `aria-pressed`.

finding: Grid cells are plain `div`s, so characters cannot be focused, read, or inserted from the keyboard. Category headers are clickable list items without a button role or expanded/collapsed state.
recommendation: Use a grid pattern with roving focus and Enter to insert. Make category headers buttons with `aria-expanded`.

finding: The accent colour on the panel background has a 4.25:1 contrast ratio, below the 4.5:1 minimum for the small uppercase category and section headings. Code-point labels are about 10 px.
recommendation: Lighten the accent for text use. Set a minimum label size.

finding: The block search box has no label. Status counts are not announced to screen readers. Copy errors use `alert()`.
recommendation: Add a label and a live status region, and replace `alert()` with inline feedback.

finding: Inserting a character moves focus to the composition pad, which opens the on-screen keyboard on iPad.
recommendation: Keep focus in the grid. Add an explicit "edit pad" action.

finding: The "Ch" column sorts identically to "Code Point". Name sorting uses `localeCompare`, so the order varies by device locale.
recommendation: Remove the duplicate sort. Sort names by code unit.

finding: No Content-Security-Policy is present. Runtime behaviour is clean (zero requests observed), but nothing enforces it.
recommendation: Add History's CSP meta (`connect-src 'none'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, fonts from `data:` only). Add a build check that searches for network and storage APIs.

finding: Font-button markup is built by inserting config values into attributes without escaping. This is build-time only, so risk is low.
recommendation: Escape attribute values, or generate the buttons in code.

finding: The markup is not XML-parseable (scripts are not CDATA-wrapped), against the standards' polyglot-markup contract.
recommendation: Add the XML-parse build check and CDATA wrapping.

finding: `replit.md` is stale. It claims XHTML 1.1, lists files that no longer exist (`02-render.js`, `03-controls.js`, `unassigned.js`), and gives outdated sizes. Code comments cite "~25 K" names (actual: 40,470). The page header hard-codes "Unicode 17.0 · 346 blocks".
recommendation: Generate version and count text at build time. Rewrite `replit.md` as a short pointer to `AGENTS.md`.
